content:
We need to build complete retrosynthesis route JSON. Inputs: we have three template searches and apply_template results giving precursors.

We need to construct route for target molecule? Not explicitly given. Likely the target is the molecule from template searches? The mapped_rxn shows product side with SMILES. For template 1914393, product SMILES is the mapped_rxn product side: after >>. That product is the target. So target SMILES: [CH3:1][O:2][c:3]1... etc. That's a complex molecule. The apply_template-1 gave precursors list: ["COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1","FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1"].

Thus first disconnection: reaction using template 1914393 with those two precursors.

Similarly template 1914394 product SMILES is after >>: [F:1][CH:2]1[CH2:3][N:4]... etc. That's maybe intermediate from previous? The apply_template-2 gave precursors: ["ClCCl","FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1"].

Template 1914395 product SMILES is after >>: [F:1][CH:2]1[CH2:3][N:4]... same as product of 1914394? Actually 1914395 product is same as 1914394 product? Let's compare: 1914394 product: [F:1][CH:2]1[CH2:3][N:4]([CH2:5][c:6]2... )... same as 1914395 product? 1914395 product: [F:1][CH:2]1[CH2:3][N:4]([CH2:5][c:6]2... )... identical. So 1914395 is maybe a different transformation (e.g., substitution of OH to F). Its precursors: ['OC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1'].

Thus we have a hierarchy: final target (from 1914393) derived from two fragments: fragment A (COc1... ) and fragment B (FC1CN...). Fragment B likely derived from further steps: maybe from template 1914394? Actually fragment B SMILES: FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1. That contains a fluorine on a piperidine ring attached to benzyl with CCl substituent. The apply_template-2 gave precursors for a product that is similar but without CCl? Wait product of 1914394 is [F]... with aromatic ring c2... no CCl. The precursor list includes "ClCCl" and "FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1". So the product is the same as fragment B but with CCl on aromatic? Actually product SMILES includes ...[c:6]2[cH:7][cH:8][c:9]([CH2:10][Cl:11])... So aromatic ring has a CH2Cl substituent. The precursor "FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1" is the same piperidine with phenyl (no CCl). And "ClCCl" is dichloromethane? Actually ClCCl is CH2Cl2. So the reaction attaches CH2Cl to aromatic ring? So product is fragment B with CCl substituent.

Thus fragment B is derived from product of 1914394? Wait product of 1914394 is the same as fragment B? Let's check: product of 1914394 includes CH2Cl substituent on aromatic. The fragment B includes CCl on aromatic? It is "FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1": aromatic ring has CCl substituent (CCl attached to phenyl). So yes fragment B matches product of 1914394. So we need to further break fragment B using template 1914394, giving precursors: "ClCCl" and "FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1". Then the second precursor "FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1" can be further broken using template 1914395, giving precursor "OC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1". That is the final leaf.

Thus the route tree:

Root molecule: target SMILES (product of 1914393). Children: reaction node with template_id 1914393, children mol nodes for two precursors: mol A (COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1) and mol B (FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1).

Mol A is leaf (no further steps). Mol B is further broken: reaction node template_id 1914394, children: mol "ClCCl" and mol "FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1". The second mol further broken: reaction node template_id 1914395, child: mol "OC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1". That leaf.

We need to output JSON with type fields.

Make sure to include smiles strings exactly as given.

Check strings: from apply_template-1: "COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1" and "FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1". Use those.

From apply_template-2: "ClCCl" and "FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1".

From apply_template-3: "OC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1".

Now construct JSON.

Root object: type "mol", smiles = target product SMILES from template 1914393 mapped_rxn product side. Need to extract product SMILES: after >> in mapped_rxn. Provided: '[CH3:1][O:2][c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][c:7]([NH:8][C:9](=[O:10])[c:11]2[n:12][n:13][nH:14][c:28]2[NH2:29])[cH:30]1'. That's the product. Remove atom mapping? Keep as is? Usually SMILES without mapping. Could keep as is but mapping may be okay. Probably keep as is. Use that string.

Thus root smiles = "[CH3][O][c]1[cH][cH][cH][c]([NH][C](=O)[c]2[n][n][nH][c]2[NH2]) [cH]1"? But better keep original with mapping? The example uses simple SMILES. Might be okay to include mapping. We'll include as given.

Now build children array with reaction node.

Reaction node: type "reaction", template_id = 1914393, children: two mol nodes.

Mol node A: type "mol", smiles "COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1".

Mol node B: type "mol", smiles "FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1", and this node will have its own children? Actually we need to embed further reaction under this mol node. The schema likely expects each mol node can have children (reactions). In example, they only have reaction node under root. But we can nest: mol node with children array containing reaction node.

Thus for mol B, include children: reaction node template_id 1914394.

That reaction node children: mol "ClCCl" and mol "FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1". The second mol will have child reaction 1914395.

Thus nested.

Construct JSON accordingly.

Let's craft.
